claims.claim: Konica Minolta Bizhub Pro C754e, large full colour laser multifunction printer
claims.evidence: Photo 0 front badge reads 'bizhub PRO C754e' with the Konica Minolta logo; the scanner, feeder and four drawers fit a floor-standing colour MFP.
Photo 0 shows it among many used copiers in a dealer yard with a stock label on the door, which fits a used import, not a new machine. No close-ups of panels or rollers.
Internal service history cannot be seen in a photo.
No power-on view, test print or copy sample is shown.
No receipt or warranty document is shown; for a used machine in a dealer yard the original maker's warranty is unlikely to still run.

risks.risk: The machine may not power on, may show service error codes, or may print with streaks.
risks.proof: A clip of it powering on to the home screen, then copying a colour page and showing the printed sheet.

risks.risk: High total page count, which sets remaining drum, fuser and transfer belt life.
risks.proof: A photo of the counter screen or a printed configuration and meter report.
risks.if_unproven: as high meter, near end of life consumables

risks.risk: Toner cartridges, drum units, fuser or hard disk may be missing or empty.
risks.proof: A photo of the opened front door showing the toner and imaging units in place, and the consumables level screen.

risks.risk: The touch panel or document feeder may be faulty.
risks.proof: A clip touching through the panel menus and feeding a stack through the document feeder.

risks.risk: Receipt and warranty may not exist or may not match this unit.
risks.proof: A photo of the receipt and warranty next to the serial plate on the back of the machine.
risks.if_unproven: as no receipt and no warranty

proof_requests: A clip of the machine powering on, then copying and printing a colour test page, with the printed sheet in shot.
A photo of the counter or meter report showing total pages printed.
A photo of the opened front door and the consumables level screen.
A photo of the serial plate with the receipt and warranty beside it, and a handwritten note with today's date.
response.reason: The make and model are read off the front badge in photo 0, so it can be priced at its worst case as a used, not proven working machine with unknown page count. Working, meter and consumables proof would raise it.
